## Section 1: Market Overview

*Assumptions: the profile does not say what Acme Advisory sells or who competes with it. The offer comes from the website research. Competitors are inferred from the category and shown as generic types. No external sources were available, so market claims rest on the research documents only. Items to confirm are flagged.*

### 1. Overview (The "Why Now?")

Small and mid-sized companies are already using AI, mostly without a plan. Staff paste client and company data into public chatbots. Leaders know they should act but face two poor options. The first is large consultancies and strategy houses, which are built and priced for enterprises. The second is generic chatbots that forget the business after every session and tie the company to one vendor. Acme Advisory replaces slow, expensive advisory and unmanaged AI use with hands-on guidance from a former product executive, plus tools the client owns.

The mission is to help leaders act faster. A leader can set an AI use policy by answering seven questions. A small team can have an AI operating system running after a one-hour setup (the site's method claim, not yet proven by customer results). A regulated firm can run AI models inside its own office, so client data never leaves. Ease of use and ownership are the design principles. Company knowledge sits in plain files the client controls, and the AI model can be swapped without losing anything. Three tools are free and open source. API access and formal integrations: Not available in the documents.

**Market size (estimates, definitions vary by source):**
- AI consulting: roughly $5B to $11B in 2025.
- Forecast growth: about 17% to 26% a year.
- Acme Advisory's serviceable market: Not available.

### 2. Trends & Shifts In The Market

| Shift Category | Description of Change | The Window of Opportunity |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Unmanaged AI use at work | Employees adopt AI before the company sets rules. The site's own line: "Your team is already using AI." | A short, usable AI policy and rollout kit gets leaders from no rules to clear rules in one sitting. It is also a free entry point to paid work. |
| Client-data privacy in regulated work | Law, accounting and mortgage firms handle confidential data and cannot send it to public AI services. Open-weight models can now run inside a firm's own network. | Private AI for firms of about 3 to 25 people is a defined offer with a named buyer. Large providers rarely serve firms this small. |
| Build in-house over buy | Leaders are questioning the "build trap" and want to build AI capability themselves rather than hand it to vendors. | Advisory and workshops that teach leaders to build their own AI chief of staff fit this shift. They deliver capability the leader keeps. |
| Model churn and vendor lock-in | Models change fast, and most chat tools forget the business after each session. | An owned, model-agnostic "company brain" in plain files keeps the knowledge and lets the client switch models without loss. |

*Gap: no regulatory or dated external sources were provided. Confirm each shift with buyer conversations before it goes on the website.*

### 3. Landscape Map & Differentiation

**Category context:** Acme Advisory sits in AI consulting and advisory, next to AI governance. It also sells small software-style tools and workshops. The site claims no single category, so the market cannot place it yet. Brand awareness is low and unmeasured. Most competitors use generic "AI strategy and transformation" language, which leaves room for a sharper, narrower claim.

| Alternate Solution | Status Quo Limitation | Core Limitation / Why We Win |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Strategy houses | Board-level brand and scale. Slow, costly and built for large enterprises. | Acme Advisory offers senior attention, faster starts and prices a small company can afford. Pricing is unpublished, so confirm this edge. |
| Large consultancies and integrators | Strong on governance, controls and delivery scale. Heavy engagements and rotating teams. | Smaller, hands-on work led by one operator who has run the function. |
| AI boutiques and fractional teams | Deep engineering and build skill. Often light on product, positioning and adoption. | Acme Advisory leads with product judgment and team adoption, not only build. |
| Solo fractional AI executives | Named senior operators with published fees. One example starts at USD 80,000 for consulting and USD 30,000 a month for a fractional seat, with a six-month minimum. Capped client counts. | Buyers below that price floor, or those wanting bounded, independent work, are underserved. |
| AI governance software | Cheap and quick for policy and compliance. Does not build capability or change how people work. | Policy plus rollout and hands-on training, with a free generator as the entry point. |
| Internal teams | Close to the business. Short on time and AI experience, and slow to start. | An experienced outside operator speeds up the first 90 days. Needs proof. |
| Public chatbots, unmanaged | Free and instant. They forget the business, expose client data and lock the company into one vendor. | Owned memory in plain files, model choice, and models that run inside the office. |

**Weak spot:** Acme Advisory has no case studies, customer logos or measured outcomes. Every "why we win" claim above is a position, not yet a proven fact. The founder's track record is the only hard-to-copy asset, and it does not scale past one person.

### Positioning Summary: The Sweet Spot

**Sweet spot (draft, founder to confirm):** Owner-led firms of about 3 to 25 people, especially regulated professional practices, that want to use AI without exposing client data and cannot afford enterprise consulting or a full-time AI executive. Acme Advisory helps them adopt AI safely in weeks. A former product executive does the work hands-on, and the client keeps the data, the files and the choice of model.

**Core edge against incumbents:**
- **Operator credibility:** the advice comes from someone who has run the function.
- **Ownership:** plain files, swappable models and private deployment, so there is no lock-in.
- **Right-sized and bounded:** clear scope and a clear buyer, priced for firms the large providers skip.

**Decision needed from the founder:** Private AI is the most defined offer, but the homepage speaks to product and revenue leaders. Pick one lead offer and one primary buyer before the website and messaging are rewritten.
